subject: Clarify: Output ownership & training safeguards on Order Form
messages:
From: Julia Wang <julia@hightower.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Aaron Reed <areed@hightower.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines + IP questions

Diego —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our legal team attached a redline and highlighted three items we need clarified before we can move forward:

1) Training: Hightower cannot agree to a broad training license. We need explicit language that Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train models or improve models in any way without prior written consent.

2) Output ownership: We expect to retain exclusive rights to outputs generated from our proprietary prompts and data; please confirm that Redwood disclaims ownership and does not assert any rights to derivative works.

3) Feedback license / telemetry: We are open to limited telemetry for service improvement, but that must be aggregated/anonymized and explicitly excluded from model training; we also want an option to opt-out of any such collection.

I've attached the redline (Hightower_redlines_OrderForm_09092027.pdf) and included short comments. Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether legal can provide proposed alternate wording? We're hoping to close this week.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Wang
Head of Partnerships | Hightower AI

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + IP questions

Julia — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Aditya (account lead) so we can get a legally-vetted counterproposal.

Quick responses up front:
- We can agree to carve out Customer-provided data and any PII/PHI from any training use by default.
- Output ownership is negotiable — we do not typically claim ownership of customer outputs, but we need limited rights to improve service quality unless the customer opts out (pricing adjustment applies).
- We can offer aggregated telemetry for product improvement but will propose explicit opt-out language.

Lauren — can you weigh in on the actual Order Form/MSA redline language? Aditya, if Hightower insists on a no-training clause, we should outline the pricing/ops implications.

Propose a 30-minute call Wednesday to resolve quickly — are you available?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + IP questions

Diego / Aditya / Julia — I reviewed Hightower's redline and sketched a practical compromise that balances their IP concerns with Redwood's need to operate and improve our service. Summary of proposed approach: 

1) Training prohibition baseline: Add a clause in the Order Form stating that Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or improve models for any third party.

2) Service improvement exception: Permit Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and system-level metrics (e.g., tokenization errors, latency histograms) for internal product improvement, expressly excluding generation outputs and any content-level data. Include an opt-out mechanism where customer can disable telemetry collection for a defined set of metrics.

3) Outputs and derivatives: Explicitly confirm that the customer retains title to Outputs generated by their prompts/data. Redwood will retain a narrow, non-exclusive right to host, cache, and serve Outputs to the customer for the duration of the Agreement; no rights to create derivative model weights.

4) Commercial alternative: Provide an optional addendum (Order Form checkbox) where the customer may permit training on anonymized, consented data for a discounted price; absent that checkbox, training is disallowed.

5) Audit / retention / deletion: Add retention windows and a deletion workflow for Customer Content and Outputs on contract termination.

I'll prepare proposed redline snippets (two versions: aggressive no-training and compromise with telemetry) and upload them. Note: if Hightower insists on a complete ban (no telemetry, no internal metrics) we need to discuss uplift which may include a premium or managed private deployment.

Proposed next step: Diego/Aditya — please confirm which deal tier applies and whether Hightower has a procurement deadline. Julia/Aaron — can you confirm if the opt-out/checkbox flow would be acceptable?

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Reed <areed@hightower.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Julia Wang <julia@hightower.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + IP questions

Lauren / Diego / Aditya — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Hightower Legal:  

- Hightower cannot accept any language that permits Redwood to use Outputs to train models, even if 'de-identified', because our outputs contain aggregated derivatives of our proprietary models and customer pipelines.
- Aggregated telemetry for infrastructure metrics is acceptable, provided it is limited to non-content diagnostics and cannot be combined with Outputs or Customer Content for model training.
- We appreciate the opt-in checkbox idea. If Redwood needs a commercial mechanism to utilize data for training, we can discuss that under a separate SOW or addendum where we would explicitly grant narrow training rights in return for pricing concessions.

We are aiming to complete order execution by the end of next week; if you can send proposed text today we can review internally. Happy to do a short call, but prefer to keep the changes in writing for legal review first.

Thanks,
Aaron Reed
Senior Counsel | Hightower AI
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Reed <areed@hightower.ai>, Julia Wang <julia@hightower.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + IP questions

Aaron / Julia — appreciate the clarity. Lauren and I discussed and drafted compromise language below that we believe addresses Hightower's main concerns while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve the platform. Please review and let us know if this conveys the intent Hightower needs. If acceptable, we'll produce a redline for the Order Form and deliver via DocuSign.

Proposed snippet (for Order Form / Schedule X):
"Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and Customer Outputs. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or improve model weights used in Redwood's production models without Customer's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect aggregated, de-identified service telemetry and system-level metrics (which shall not include Customer Outputs or content-level data) for the sole purpose of improving operational stability and product performance, unless Customer elects the Opt-Out by checking the 'Disable Telemetry' box in the Order Form. Any use of Customer Data or Outputs for model training will be subject to a separate, explicit written agreement.

If that looks correct, Lauren will incorporate this into a redline. Note one operational caveat: fully disabling telemetry will limit some platform insights (latency/cost optimizations) and may impact our ability to offer certain performance guarantees; if Hightower requires full telemetry disablement we will need to document the corresponding service-level and pricing adjustments.

Next steps:
- Lauren to produce redline and upload to the Workdocs link (https://redwood.my.workdocs/htwr/contract-draft-v3).
- If acceptable, we'll move to DocuSign (DocuSign://envelope/HTWR-ENVELOPE-2027-09).
- Diego / Aditya to confirm any commercial uplift and whether a private deployment option is required.

Would Monday at 10am PT work for a short sync if you have lingering questions?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
